propositions: Plan review must own a new criterion that detects contradictions within a single ticket's acceptance criteria, scope declarations, and out-of-scope exemptions, to catch unsatisfiable commitments before implementation rather than at completion verification.

A new 1-TURN criterion ac-satisfiability (facet coherence, default advisory) must recognize three contradiction patterns: universal-vs-carve-out (scope exempts a set member an AC quantifies over), derived-artifact closure (AC asserts a property of a regenerated artifact whose source negates it), and snapshot cardinality (AC pins a count for a set the plan says is discovered at runtime).

G3's child-coverage audit cannot fire because the sibling roster it receives carries only ids and titles; it must be enriched with each child's acceptance-criteria items extracted via evaluate_plan_clarity().ac_items so G3 can verify that no sibling covers each parent criterion.

The sibling roster is currently built by three independent code copies in pass1.py, fidelity_spot_eval.py, and eval_solver.py; they must be unified into a single build_sibling_roster helper called from all three to prevent eval paths from sending title-only rosters while production sends AC-bearing ones, which would corrupt dogfooding data.

The sibling roster must move from per-pairing instructions into the byte-stable system prompt prefix to avoid re-sending the full child acceptance-criteria corpus once per pairing (quadratic in child count), and its token cost must be included in parent_tokens estimation for accurate bin-packing and warm-gate decisions.

The rendered roster format must place each child's acceptance-criteria items indented under its `- <id>: <title>` line, degrade gracefully for children with no parseable AC section, and be reflected in G3's rubric so the audit can test the no-sibling-covers-it rule against actual acceptance criteria rather than titles alone.
